parts.text: A student investigates potential difference in an electric circuit and determines the resistance of an unknown resistor X. The student assembles the circuit shown in Figure 3.1. The circuit consists of a resistor X connected in series with a resistor of resistance R = 10 Ω. Figure 3.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The student: • closes the switch • connects a voltmeter in parallel with resistor X • measures the potential difference (p.d.) V across resistor X • opens the switch.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) On Figure 3.1, draw the voltmeter connected to measure the p.d. across resistor X. [1]

ms.label: 3(a)(i)
ms.text: voltmeter connected in parallel with X

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The voltmeter reading is shown in Figure 3.2. Figure 3.2 Record the voltmeter reading V in the second column of Table 3.1 for R = 10 Ω. Table 3.1 resistance R / Ω p.d. V / V 1 V 1 V / 10 15 1.6 18 1.5 22 1.3 33 1.0 [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student repeats 3(a) by replacing the 10 Ω resistor with resistors of resistance R = 15 Ω, 18 Ω, 22 Ω and 33 Ω in turn. The student records the values of V in Table 3.1. Calculate the value of 1 V for each value of V. Record your values of 1 V in Table 3.1 to 2 significant figures. [2]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of 1 V 1 V / (y-axis) against R / Ω (x-axis). Start your axes at the origin (0,0). Draw a best-fit straight line. 0 0 [4]

parts.text: (d) Determine the gradient G of your line. Show all your working and indicate on the graph the values you use. G = ......................................................... [1]

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) The resistance R X of resistor X can be calculated using the equation: R X = c G . Use your answers to 3(d) and 3(e) to calculate R X . Record your answer to the nearest ohm. R X = ...................................................... Ω [1]
